# RFC-0001: Single-tool model deployment service

> **Version:** 0.2.1 | **Status:** normative | **Phase:** test
> **Owners:** @Tyler Michael Smith

---

## 1. Summary

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0001:C-TOOL-SURFACE] Single-tool surface (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-tool-surface"></a>

The model-deployment MCP server MUST advertise exactly one entry in MCP `tools/list`, named `deploy_model`. Its input schema MUST be a closed JSON object with required property `manifesto_config` and no other properties. `manifesto_config` MUST be a string whose UTF-8 encoding is from 1 through 1,048,576 bytes and MUST contain exactly one llm-manifesto model configuration YAML document. Tool annotations MUST set `readOnlyHint` to false, `destructiveHint` to false, `idempotentHint` to true, and `openWorldHint` to true. Server instructions MUST state that a successful call returns a ready endpoint, that the caller controls model deployment intent through Manifesto configuration, and that the target environment remains operator-controlled.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0001:C-OPERATOR-CATALOG] Operator-controlled render context (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-operator-catalog"></a>

The service MUST authenticate and authorize the caller before parsing `manifesto_config`; authentication or authorization denial MUST be a protocol-level error and MUST prevent tool invocation. YAML parsing MUST accept exactly one document, MUST reject duplicate mapping keys, aliases, non-standard or custom tags, and a parsed representation exceeding 10,000 scalar, sequence, and mapping nodes in total, and MUST use only the schema implemented by the operator-pinned renderer. Before rendering, the service MUST reject every parsed field that the renderer recognizes as selecting or referencing a namespace, Kubernetes context or cluster profile, credential or Secret, deployment user or identity, cache or log root, routing profile, or submission policy. As the sole exception, the renderer-required top-level Manifesto `release` field MAY be absent or present for schema compatibility; the service MUST ignore any submitted value, remove it from deployment identity input, and set `release` to the derived `deployment_id` before rendering. All parser, bound, forbidden-field, unknown-field, unresolved-inheritance, and render-context rejections MUST return `INVALID_MANIFESTO_CONFIG` before cluster mutation. The service MUST render accepted model intent with an operator-controlled immutable renderer version, cluster profile, Kubernetes context, namespace, deployment identity policy, credentials, routing policy, storage roots, and submission policy.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0001:C-DEPLOYMENT] Idempotent ready deployment (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-deployment"></a>

`deploy_model` MUST compute `manifesto_digest` as lowercase SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 byte sequence of `manifesto_config`. It MUST derive a stable `deployment_id` from an unambiguous versioned deterministic encoding of the accepted parsed model intent with the top-level `release` field removed, together with the operator-controlled render-context identity. Configurations whose accepted parsed forms differ only in `release` MUST derive the same `deployment_id`. Before rendering, the service MUST set `release` to that derived identity whether the field was absent or supplied. The service MUST render and fully validate the resulting Kubernetes resources against the target environment before creating resources. Rendering MUST produce exactly one externally reported inference endpoint, potentially backed by multiple role workloads, or fail as `INVALID_MANIFESTO_CONFIG` before mutation. Render or validation failure MUST leave cluster state unchanged. Sequential or concurrent calls with the same deployment intent and render context MUST converge on one owned resource set and MUST NOT create another logical deployment. The service MUST create or observe only resources bearing the service ownership identity and derived `deployment_id`; it MUST fail before changing a rendered resource that exists without matching ownership and desired-state identity, and it MUST NOT delete, adopt, replace, or change any existing resource. A successful call MUST mean that every rendered model workload reports ready and that a probe of the exact externally reported inference endpoint succeeds before an operator-configured finite timeout. Any failure after the current call causes the target to accept an owned resource MUST include `deployment_id`, MUST NOT trigger automatic rollback, MAY leave only that deployment owned resources in place, and a retry MUST reconcile the same rendered resource set.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0001:C-RESULT] Bounded result (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-result"></a>

A successful `deploy_model` call MUST return `isError: false` and `structuredContent` matching a closed JSON object with required properties: `schema_version`, the string constant `1`; `manifesto_digest`, the lowercase SHA-256 digest over the exact submitted `manifesto_config` UTF-8 bytes; `deployment_id`, a non-empty string no longer than 253 characters; `endpoint`, the exact absolute URI probed by the service, no longer than 2,048 characters; `ready`, the boolean constant true; `target_namespace`, a non-empty string no longer than 63 characters; and `resources`, an array of at most 64 closed objects. Each resource object MUST require string properties `api_version`, `kind`, and `name`, each from 1 through 253 characters. The result MUST NOT contain the submitted Manifesto configuration, rendered manifests, logs, credentials, or other unbounded content.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0001:C-ERRORS] Failure behavior (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-errors"></a>

Authentication or authorization denial MUST use a protocol-level error before tool invocation and MUST NOT parse, include, or diagnose `manifesto_config`. A recognized `deploy_model` domain failure MUST return an MCP tool result with `isError: true` and `structuredContent` matching a closed JSON object with required properties `schema_version`, the string constant `1`; `code`, one of `INVALID_MANIFESTO_CONFIG`, `INVALID_OPERATOR_CONFIGURATION`, `TARGET_VALIDATION_FAILED`, `APPLY_FAILED`, `READINESS_TIMEOUT`, or `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`; `message`, a string from 1 through 1,024 Unicode characters; `retryable`, a boolean; and `deployment_id`, either null or a non-empty string no longer than 253 characters. `INVALID_MANIFESTO_CONFIG`, `INVALID_OPERATOR_CONFIGURATION`, and `TARGET_VALIDATION_FAILED` MUST set `retryable` to false and `deployment_id` to null. `READINESS_TIMEOUT` MUST set `retryable` to true. `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` MUST set `retryable` to true and MUST set `deployment_id` to null before target acceptance during the current call or to the derived deployment identifier after target acceptance during the current call. `APPLY_FAILED` MUST set `retryable` according to whether repeating the same rendered deployment can make progress. Every failure after target acceptance during the current call, including `APPLY_FAILED` and `READINESS_TIMEOUT`, MUST include `deployment_id`. Malformed MCP requests and unknown tools MUST use protocol-level errors instead. Error content MUST NOT expose the submitted Manifesto configuration, credentials, internal stack traces, or unbounded dependency output.

*Since: v0.1.0*

## 3. Overview

### [RFC-0001:C-PURPOSE] Purpose and scope (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-purpose"></a>

This RFC defines a dedicated MCP service for the smallest useful model-deployment workflow: an authorized caller supplies one complete llm-manifesto model configuration and receives a ready inference endpoint. Deployment discovery, arbitrary Kubernetes manifests, cluster selection, status management, scaling, and deletion are outside this initial contract.

*Since: v0.1.0*
